subject: G-203-011 Week 4 recap
body:
Hi Priya,

Quick recap of today's Week 4 for G-203-011. Her Baseline was Mon 14 Sep.

She got in at 7:40. Per her diary, yesterday's dose went down at 8:30 am at home. Predose PK drawn at 7:55. Then vitals, SVC, hand-held dynamometry, ALSFRS-R, C-SSRS, 12-lead ECG and safety labs. Urine pregnancy negative. Contraception reviewed: copper IUD, and her husband uses condoms every time. Documented in the CRF.

Once everything was finished, Marcus mixed her two packets into applesauce with a little thickener. I checked her ID and the kit number against IRT before he handed it to her. She finished it in about 10 minutes, dose time 8:40. Postdose PK drawn at 11:10.

She brought back all her cartons. Packet count matched her diary, no missed doses. Dispensed 4 new cartons and reminded her to bring everything back next time.

Dana

Leah

subject: Con med review - G-209-007 (Week 8)
body:
Hi all,

I went through the medication list for G-209-007 at yesterday's chart review. All okay to continue. Notes for the file:

1. Rosuvastatin 10 mg daily (long-standing). I consider it wide therapeutic index for him. I talked it over with the medical monitor last week. We will watch for muscle pain and check CK with the safety labs.
2. Famotidine 20 mg twice daily for reflux. Wide therapeutic index. Continue and watch for side effects.
3. Buspirone 10 mg twice daily for anxiety. Wide therapeutic index in my view. He knows to tell us if the anxiety comes back, since the study drug can lower buspirone levels.
4. Itraconazole 200 mg daily for 14 days, started 1 Oct by his PCP for oral thrush. It is a CYP3A inhibitor, not an inducer.
5. Modafinil 100 mg each morning for fatigue, started 20 Sep. Our pharmacist checked the Flockhart table: it is a moderate CYP3A inducer, not a strong one.

Please log all of these in the con med page if they aren't there already.

Dr. Okafor

body:

Dr. Lin decided to drop him to one packet a day starting Tue 17 Nov for two weeks, then reassess. She'll mention it to the medical monitor on the monthly call in December. No PK sample was drawn, since his next PK isn't due until Week 16.

AE entered as severe orthostatic dizziness, action: dose reduced. He felt better by Wednesday.

Thanks,
Dana

subject: SAE - G-217-003 seizure
body:

She was kept overnight for observation, so we reported it as an SAE within 24 hours of hearing about it.

She feels okay now, just tired. Since she was eligible when she enrolled, we plan to keep her on study drug along with the new phenytoin. Her next visit is Week 12 by phone on 14 Dec.

In-person ET visit was Fri 18 Dec: vitals, SVC, strength, ALSFRS-R, ECG, safety labs, endocrine panel, biomarkers, C-SSRS, ALSAQ-40, CNS-BFS, exit questionnaire and vital status. We skipped ROADS, PGI-C, PGI-S and CGI-C, since those are for people completing Week 24. No LP: he had no baseline CSF. His wife is post-menopausal.

His follow-up safety call was yesterday, Thu 28 Jan. We couldn't reach him over the holidays. No new AEs.

Leah

subject: Med list check - three participants
body:
Hi team,

I reviewed three medication lists this week:

G-248-003 (randomized September): his PCP started rifampin on Mon 30 Nov for latent TB, a 4-month course. He's tolerating it well. Okay to continue both.

G-248-008: quetiapine 25 mg at bedtime for sleep. I consider it wide therapeutic index at this dose. Continue, and watch for sleep getting worse.

G-248-010: methotrexate 15 mg weekly for rheumatoid arthritis. I consider it narrow therapeutic index for her. Her last dose before starting was Thu 26 Nov, and her first study dose was Mon 30 Nov. She continues her weekly methotrexate; her rheumatologist is monitoring her counts.

Dr. Okafor

subject: holiday week visits - G-249-012 wk 16
body:

subject: Kit mix-up and a storage note
body:
Hi team,

Two pharmacy items.

1. At yesterday's visit we found that on Mon 7 Dec, G-250-012 was handed the cartons assigned in IRT to G-250-014. They were picked up at the same time and the bags got swapped. She took that supply for 4 weeks. Both are blinded, and she's fine, so I corrected it in IRT, gave her the right cartons, and moved on. No need to escalate.

2. On Wednesday night the cartons for Thursday's visits were left on the counter in exam room 3 overnight instead of going back to the drug room. The room isn't locked, but the clinic was closed. Temperature would have been normal room temperature.

Ken
